newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser to reveal cost-cutting plans.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser to reveal cost-cutting plans.

text.p: Loss-making British department store chain House of Fraser Plc, due to report on Christmas trading on Monday, is likely to use the occasion to reveal the results of a sweeping business review, which could include store closures and job cuts, industry sources said.

Retail analysts said they believed the retailer, which made a first half loss of 13.6 million stg, would probably give details of a restructuring which was likely to rationalise its store portfolio, cut costs and write-down unwanted stock.

In October, when House of Fraser published half-year results, it estimated it would need to make provisions of between 40 and 50 million stg in its full-year accounts to pay for possible store closures, job cuts and stock write-downs.

At the time there was speculation that as many as 1,000 jobs could go, and since then press reports have suggested around six of the group's 51 stores could be earmarked for closure. A company spokesman declined to comment.

In October chief executive John Coleman, brought in last April in a top management shake-up, said the company planned to strip out surplus costs, sell off unwanted stock and close or sell stores which would be unprofitable over the long term.
The group has been beset by problems since its flotation in 1994. The stores have had troubles with stock management and poor sales of its "own bought" ranges in womenswear.
Retail analysts expected a fairly detailed statement on the strategic review as well as an update on sales over Christmas.
The performance over Christmas is expected to follow the pattern of other retailers, with business slow in early December, but stronger in Christmas week. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
